Commentary.Commentary: Around 61 overs left in the day. Can New Zealand do better in the second dig? Will this match end today? Stay tuned for the third innings...

Pakistan well, used the conditions perfectly to their advantage. The track was spinning big time and Yasir Shah exploited that to the fullest. His 8/41 is his personal best in Tests and he would be looking to add more to that tally. None of the other bowlers were required much but they did their bit.

A forgettable passage of play for the Kiwis. After playing so well in Abu Dhabi, they have been completely bowled over here in Dubai. They started well, adding 50 for the opening wicket but then lost flow completely. There were 6 ducks in the innings, with only the top 3 managing double figures.
Will the follow-on be enforced? Pakistan have had to bowl only 35.3 overs, that too, 9 were bowled last evening. Yes, we have the confirmation. PAKISTAN HAVE ENFORCED THE FOLLOW-ON.

Floated outside off, Boult comes down the track to defend but the ball spins away and he is nowhere near the pitch of the ball. Sarfraz collects and furiously whips off the bails. PAKISTAN GET A LEAD OF 328!

An hour ago, we were all thinking this is going to be a draw. But with Yasir spinning the ball so much and exposing the Kiwi middle order, it seems like Pakistan will be batting today itself. A result looks very much possible. The Black Caps will hope for some riposte post Lunch. Join us back at 1.10 pm local (0910 GMT) for the second session.

First, he got Raval off a fortuitous edge from the back of the bat and then ripped out three in an over to leave the Kiwis in dire straights.

The Pakistan fielders were rushing across to get one more over before the break but it was not to be so. The umpires have called for Lunch. New Zealand will heave a sigh of relief. What a horrific session for them.

The players are out in the middle! Here are the revised session timings - 1100-1230, 1310-1510 and 1530-1800. All timings in local. Out come the overnight batsmen. Mohammad Abbas to start off proceedings for the morning. Latham to face. Here we go!
1030 local -  Hurrah! The weather seems to have cleared up and we could have a resumption soon!

START OF PLAY DELAYED DUE TO RAIN! Are we in Colombo? Naahh... this is from Dubai. The news is that there was a heavy deluge last night and because of that, well, it is absolutely pleasant to play. But unfortunately, the ground is absolutely damp and the pitch is covered. Ramiz Raja reckons that once the rain stops, play should commence within half an hour. Simon Doull looks at the forecast and predicts play to resume within an hour and a half. So that means, effectively a session lost. Let's hope for the best. Please stay tuned for updates.

We are into Day 3 now and the pitch is starting to turn but it is slow. With so much time already taken out of the game, the Black Caps only need to ensure that they try and bat till Lunch tomorrow. Only Pakistan can win from here by the looks of it, but the more time they spend on the field, the difficulty level will rise to enforce a result. Remember, New Zealand are the ones who are 1-0 up and a draw here will ensure that they do not lose the series.

Pakistan, not surprisingly, chose to bat after winning the toss but could not quite press on the advantage. One can understand a cautious start after losing two quick wickets but not even going at 3 runs per over in spite of being set is baffling to understand. Azhar Ali, Haris Sohail and Babar Azam basked in the Dubai sun and the poor Kiwi bowlers barring that first hour on Day 1, got nothing much from the pitch.

Huh? Is it already time? Yawnnnn.... hello and a drowsy welcome to the third day of the second Test between Pakistan and New Zealand in Dubai. This type of a welcome is because of the way this game has enveloped so far. 176 overs, 442 runs and just 5 wickets. An average of 70 runs per session. It has been nothing short of a snooze fest.
Snooozeeeeeeee..... snooozeeeeeee........... snooozeeeee..... TRRINNNNNGGGGGGGGGGGG! TRRINNNNNNNNNNNNNGGGGGGGGGGGGG! TRINNNNNNNNNNNNNNNG!
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

The Kiwis, on the other hand, will need partnerships. They will want their experience players to share the responsibility on a wicket which is turning but is still good to bat on. Day 3 is often called the 'moving day' of a Test match and that should give us an idea as to which direction this game is heading. Join us for all the action at 1000 local (0600 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye.

It was a day dominated by batsmen! Just the sole wicket of Haris Sohail fell today. Pakistan, courtesy 100s from Sohail and Azam and a massive 186-run stand, have put up a very good first innings total. However, the pace at which they batted has already taken a lot of time out of this Test match. They will now need their bowlers to step up and they will hope to bundle New Zealand out cheaply.
New Zealand have survived the nervy period and will head into Day 3 without any damage being done to them. Their batters though still have a lot of work left.
